category: PCB Layout: Technology menu, pad/via technology, routing controls, inspectors and manufacturing output options
description: PCB Layout features beyond the mode-level entries: Technology-menu configuration (layer pairs, board properties, grids, teardropping), the Design Rule Manager's net-class and board-global rules and the rule hierarchy, keepouts, pad-style creation and padstack technology (offset holes, non-functional pads, resin-filled vias, micro-vias), the Via and Zone inspectors, zone stitching and plane fill options, testpoints, the push-and-shove routing controls (Route Command Centre, Visual DRC, auto-complete, layer/neck toggles), length-match and diff-pair viewers, editing commands (replicate, align/distribute, lock, move-to, selection filter, colour sets), output-origin and Gerber/Excellon dialogue options, pre-production check, panelisation, assembly drawings, IPC-D-356, multi-board commands, 3D model attachment and the autorouter command language.

tools.name: Technology > Layer Pairs (Edit Layer Pairs)
tools.description: Defines which copper layers are paired so that pressing the space bar while routing swaps to the partner layer and drops a via in one action, and tells the autorouter which layer pairs to use for multi-layer boards (the same assignment appears per net class in the Design Rule Manager). On a two-layer board Top/Bottom is the only pair; on six layers you might pair Top with Inner 1 and Bottom with Inner 4.
tools.usage: PCB Layout > Technology > Layer Pairs > choose the partner for each copper layer > OK

parameters.name: Layer / partner layer
parameters.description: Mapping used by the space-bar layer toggle and via placement.

tools.example: Pair Top Copper with Inner 1 so escape routing from a BGA drops blind vias to the first inner layer with a single space-bar press.
tools.notes: Via drill spans come from the Layer Stackup; a pair whose span is not defined cannot be joined with a via.

tools.name: Technology > Board Properties
tools.description: Sets the physical extent used as the board's working area before an edge is drawn - width and height (e.g. 175mm x 100mm) - together with board-level options such as the default board origin, so the edge can be drawn accurately and the grid/coordinate display reflect the real board size. The board edge itself is then drawn on the Board Edge layer with the 2D graphics tools.
tools.usage: PCB Layout > Technology > Board Properties > width/height (units mm or th) > OK

parameters.name: Width / Height
parameters.description: Board size; type the units (mm or th) with the value.

tools.example: Set 175mm x 100mm, then draw the Board Edge rectangle and move the origin to its bottom-left corner.
tools.notes: Board size also drives the autorouter's working area and power plane limits.

tools.name: Technology > Grid Configuration (Grids)
tools.description: Configures the PCB module's snap grids and preferred units: the imperial and metric snap values available on the View menu/keyboard (e.g. 5th, 25th, 50th, 100th or 0.1mm, 0.5mm, 1mm), the displayed grid pitch and the default unit system (the M key toggles between them). Fine snap for SMT pad work, coarse snap for placement.
tools.usage: PCB Layout > Technology > Grid Configuration > set snap values and default units > OK; View menu or Ctrl+F1..F4 to switch snaps

parameters.name: Snap values
parameters.description: Four selectable snaps per unit system.

parameters.name: Default units
parameters.description: Imperial (th) or metric (mm).

tools.example: Set metric 0.1/0.25/0.5/1mm snaps for a board with 0.5mm-pitch QFPs.
tools.notes: Grid colour and visibility are set in the Displayed Layers dialogue (View menu).

tools.name: Technology > Set Teardropping (teardrops and track tapers)
tools.description: Dialogue that enables dynamic teardrops and track tapers: the maximum annular ring below which a pad/via receives a teardrop, the teardrop length, whether SMT pads are included, and the preferred taper length (as a percentage) applied where a track changes width. Teardrops are generated dynamically as routes are completed and only where design rules allow; a per-pad override lives in the Edit Single Pin dialogue.
tools.usage: PCB Layout > Technology > Set Teardropping > enable, max annular ring, length, SMT option, taper % > OK

parameters.name: Maximum annular ring
parameters.description: Pads with smaller rings get teardrops.

parameters.name: Teardrop length
parameters.description: Extent of the fillet along the track.

parameters.name: Taper length %
parameters.description: Track-width transition taper (8.14).

tools.example: Enable teardrops with 10th max ring and 20th length to protect 0.3mm drills from breakout on a dense board.
tools.notes: Part of the Advanced Feature Set (PCB Design Level 2+). A teardrop that would violate a rule is simply not created.

tools.name: Design Rule Manager > Net Classes tab (trace, via and neck styles, layer assignment)
tools.description: The second tab of the Design Rule Manager: for each net class (POWER, SIGNAL, BUS and user classes such as ANSW) it sets the trace style used when routing (e.g. T8, T15, T30), the via style, the optional neck style used when Shift+N thins the track through obstacles, the ratsnest colour/visibility, and the layer assignment pairs the autorouter may use for the class. The status bar shows the class's style and width during routing.
tools.usage: Technology > Design Rule Manager > Net Classes tab > select class > Trace Style / Neck Style / Via Style / Layer pairs / Ratsnest colour > OK

parameters.name: Trace Style
parameters.description: Default track style (width) for the class.

parameters.name: Neck Style
parameters.description: Thinner style toggled with Shift+N.

parameters.name: Via Style
parameters.description: Via pad/drill for the class.

parameters.name: Layer assignment pairs
parameters.description: Autorouter layers for the class.

tools.example: POWER: T30 trace, V80 via; ANSW: T15 trace, T15 neck, smaller via; SIGNAL: T8 trace, T8 neck.
tools.notes: Classes are created on the schematic with CLASS= labels; they appear here after netlisting.

tools.name: Solder Resist Guard and Minimum Solder Dam rules
tools.description: Two board-global manufacturing rules in the Design Rule Manager beyond the copper clearances: Solder Resist Guard (Resist->Copper) enforces a clearance between the resist opening of a pad and neighbouring copper, so tracks running too close to a pad's guard gap are flagged; Minimum Solder Dam (Resist->Resist, added in 8.14) enforces the minimum resist web between adjacent pad openings. Violations are cured by moving the trace or by reducing the pad style's guard gap.
tools.usage: Technology > Design Rule Manager > Design Rules tab > board global rules: Solder Resist Guard, Minimum Solder Dam > values

parameters.name: Solder Resist Guard
parameters.description: Resist-to-copper clearance.

parameters.name: Minimum Solder Dam
parameters.description: Minimum resist width between openings.

tools.example: Set a 4th solder dam so 0.5mm-pitch QFP pads keep individual resist windows rather than a gang opening.
tools.notes: The edge/slot clearance field on the same tab governs power planes against the board edge.

tools.name: Design rule hierarchy (board global > layer > net class > room)
tools.description: How clearances resolve: the DEFAULT rule applies to all layers and all net classes; additional rules can be limited to a specific layer, a specific net class, a specific region (design rule room) or a combination, and the most specific applicable rule wins; rooms inherit any clearance they do not override from the level above. Understanding the hierarchy avoids unexpected DRC results when several rules overlap.
tools.usage: Technology > Design Rule Manager > Design Rules tab > New Rule > scope (layer / net class / room) > clearances; tree view shows inheritance

parameters.name: Scope
parameters.description: Layer, net class and/or room the rule applies to.

parameters.name: Clearances
parameters.description: Pad-pad, pad-trace, trace-trace, graphics, edge/slot values.

tools.example: Board default 10th; rule 'HV' for net class HV 40th on all layers; room 'BGA' 5th on inner layers only - a HV net inside the BGA room still uses 40th because the class rule is more specific for that net.
tools.notes: Rooms also carry via-style overrides and exclusion zones from 9.2.

tools.name: Keepout areas (Keepout layer graphics)
tools.description: Areas where routing, placement or copper must not appear are defined by drawing 2D graphics (box, circle, path) on the Keepout layer; they apply to all layers by default but can be restricted to specific layers after placement. The DRC reports PAD-EDGE/TRACE-EDGE style violations for objects too close to the keepout, which can be ignored deliberately (the keepout has no connectivity effect) or resolved with a design rule room.
tools.usage: 2D Graphics Box mode > layer selector = Keepout > draw around the area > edit to restrict layers

parameters.name: Layers
parameters.description: All layers (default) or a chosen subset.

tools.example: Keepout box under the crystal so no tracks pass beneath it; a second keepout around a temperature sensor where a thermal-isolation slot will be milled.
tools.notes: Keepouts also bound the autorouter and power-plane fills.

tools.name: Library > New Pad Style (pad style dialogue)
tools.description: Creates a pad style available in the Object Selector: choose the pad type (circular, square, DIL, rectangular/SMT, polygonal, edge connector), set the pad diameter/size, drill mark (size of the mark in a drill plot), drill hole diameter, guard gap (solder-mask expansion) and paste-mask settings, and decide whether the style is added permanently to the defaults (Update Defaults) or kept local to this design (Local Edit). The 'C' button above the Object Selector opens the same dialogue.
tools.usage: PCB Layout > Library > New Pad Style > Name (e.g. C-180-M3) > Type > Diameter, Drill Mark, Drill Hole, Guard Gap > Update Defaults / Local Edit > OK

parameters.name: Type
parameters.description: Circular / square / DIL / rectangular SMT / polygonal / edge.

parameters.name: Diameter / size
parameters.description: Pad dimensions.

parameters.name: Drill Mark / Drill Hole
parameters.description: Plot mark size and actual hole diameter.

parameters.name: Guard Gap
parameters.description: Resist expansion beyond the pad.

tools.example: Mounting hole C-180-M3: circular through-hole, 180th diameter, 30th drill mark, 3mm hole, 20th guard gap; then place it from the circular PTH pad icon.
tools.notes: Type values directly rather than using the spin controls; keep the naming convention so styles stay readable.

tools.name: Pad style naming convention (<TYPE>-<SIZE>-<HOLE>, M prefix for metric)
tools.description: Library pad styles follow a readable format: type letter (C circular, S square, D DIL, R rectangular SMT, P polygonal, E edge), then diameter/size, then hole, in thou unless a value is prefixed with M for millimetres - so C-40-15 is a 40th circular pad with a 15th hole, C-200-M3 a 0.2in pad with a 3mm hole, and M0.5x1.8 a 0.5 x 1.8mm SMT pad. Trace and via styles use T<width> (T8, T15, T30) and V<size> (V50, V80).
tools.usage: Read/choose styles in the Object Selector by name; follow the convention when creating new ones
tools.example: A pad for a 1mm pin needs a hole of ~1.2mm: look for C-80-M1.2 or create it.
tools.notes: Consistent naming makes the Gerber aperture list and DRC messages self-explanatory.

tools.name: Padstacks (per-layer pad definitions, offset holes and slots)
tools.description: A padstack is a pad style whose shape differs per layer - larger on outer layers, minimal or absent annular rings on inner layers to maximise routing space, with separate resist and paste definitions. Proteus 9.2 added offset holes and slots, where the drill or slot is displaced from the pad origin (USB receptacles, right-angle connectors), preserved correctly through Gerber X2 output.
tools.usage: Library > New Pad Style > padstack type > define the pad per layer (Top, Inner, Bottom, resist, paste) > hole/slot size and offset

parameters.name: Per-layer shapes
parameters.description: Outer, inner, resist and paste geometry.

parameters.name: Hole / slot offset
parameters.description: X/Y displacement of the drill from the pad centre (9.2).

tools.example: USB-C receptacle: rectangular pads with slots offset 0.3mm toward the board edge.
tools.notes: Padstacks 'facilitate maximum routing area on inner layers' per the ARES documentation.

tools.name: Non-functional pads (via annular ring removal)
tools.description: Added in 8.12: annular rings on vias (and through-hole pads) can be removed on inner layers where no connection is made, gaining clearance in dense inner-layer routing; if a track later connects on that layer the ring is restored automatically. Configured per via style/design rule and honoured by the Gerber output.
tools.usage: Edit the via style / Technology settings > enable non-functional pad removal on inner layers; the DRC keeps rings where connections exist
tools.example: A 6-layer board with a 0.8mm-pitch BGA: removing unused inner rings on escape vias lets two tracks pass between vias on Inner 2.
tools.notes: Some fabricators prefer rings retained - agree it with the manufacturer.

tools.name: Resin-filled and capped vias (NCVF via-in-pad)
tools.description: Since 8.14 a via can be designated as resin filled and capped (non-conductive via fill, IPC-4761 type VII) so it can sit in an SMT pad without wicking solder; the attribute is carried into the Gerber X2 fileset/drill data so the fabricator applies the fill and cap process to those holes only.
tools.usage: Via style / Edit via > tick 'Resin filled and capped' (NCVF); use in pads of BGA/QFN fanouts
tools.example: Via-in-pad under a 0.5mm BGA: mark the fanout vias NCVF and verify the attribute in the Gerber X2 output.
tools.notes: Fill/cap raises fabrication cost; use only where needed.

tools.name: Micro-vias and 1+n+1 HDI stackup
tools.description: Proteus 9.2 adds full HDI support with the 1+n+1 board style: the Layer Stackup wizard distinguishes laser-drilled micro-via spans (outer layer to the adjacent inner layer) from mechanically drilled spans, routing can place micro-vias from the layer pairs, via barrel depth is computed from the stackup for length matching, and the drill table in the Gerber X2 output lists the micro-via passes separately.
tools.usage: Technology > Layer Stackup wizard > board style 1+n+1 > define laser micro-via spans and the mechanical core spans > route with the micro-via drill span selected

parameters.name: Board style
parameters.description: Standard or 1+n+1 HDI.

parameters.name: Micro-via span
parameters.description: Laser-drilled outer-to-inner layer pass.

tools.example: 8-layer 1+6+1 board: laser vias Top->Inner1 and Bottom->Inner6, mechanical through and buried Inner1->Inner6.
tools.notes: Requires PCB Design Level 2+ (advanced feature set).

tools.name: Via Inspector
tools.description: Introduced in Proteus 9.0: a dockable analysis tool listing every via on the board with its net, style, drill span, layers, fill attributes and position, with filtering and tagging, so via usage can be audited (unexpected through vias on an HDI board, oversized vias on high-speed nets) and corrected in bulk from the list.
tools.usage: PCB Layout > Via mode > Via Inspector icon above the parts bin (or View menu) > filter by net/style/span > select rows to tag/edit

parameters.name: Filter
parameters.description: Net class, style, span, layer.

tools.example: Filter for span Top-Bottom on the SIGNAL class and change them all to the smaller V50 style.
tools.notes: Companion of the Zone Inspector; both live in the parts-bin area of their mode.

tools.name: Zone Inspector
tools.description: Added in 8.13: an analysis and management window for power planes/zones listing each zone with its net, layer, priority, fill style, clearance, relief settings and island/nesting status; zones can be located and tagged from the list, filtered, and edited directly (net, priority, hatch, relief) without hunting for their borders on the board.
tools.usage: PCB Layout > Zone mode > Zone Inspector icon above the parts bin > select a zone > Edit / Locate

parameters.name: Zone properties
parameters.description: Net, layer, priority, fill (solid/hatched), clearance, thermal relief, stitching.

tools.example: Find the split analogue-ground zone whose priority is lower than the digital ground zone and raise it so it wins the overlap.
tools.notes: Live zone regeneration is 'orders of magnitude faster' in Proteus 9 than in 8.

tools.name: Zone stitching and picket-fence shielding
tools.description: Context-menu commands on a zone (added in 8.7): automated stitching places a grid of vias through a zone connecting it to the same net on other layers (row/column pitch, via style, edge inset), and picket-fence shielding places a via fence around the zone's boundary (or along a high-speed route, since routes gained the same isolation options) to contain EMI and define return paths.
tools.usage: Right-click a zone > Stitch zone (pitch, via style) / Shield zone (fence spacing); right-click a route > shielding options

parameters.name: Pitch / spacing
parameters.description: Distance between stitching or fence vias.

parameters.name: Via style
parameters.description: Style used for the generated vias.

tools.example: Stitch the top and bottom GND pours at 5mm pitch and fence the RF trace with 1mm-spaced ground vias.
tools.notes: Generated vias obey the design rules and the zone clearance.

tools.name: Power plane fill options (solid, hatched, diagonal cross-hatch, circular/octagonal thermal holes)
tools.description: Zone/plane configuration options: solid or hatched fill with hatch pitch and width, diagonal cross-hatch (added in 8.10), thermal relief type (spoke count/width) and whether relief/clearance holes are octagonal or circular (8.10), plus zone priority, clearance override and island removal. Multiple planes per layer (e.g. analogue and digital ground) and user-drawn planes of specific dimensions are part of the professional feature set.
tools.usage: Zone mode > place/edit zone > Edit Zone dialogue > Net, Layer, Type (Solid/Hatched/Diagonal), Relief (thermal, holes circular/octagonal), Clearance, Priority

parameters.name: Fill type
parameters.description: Solid, hatched, diagonal cross-hatch.

parameters.name: Relief holes
parameters.description: Circular or octagonal clearance/relief shapes.

parameters.name: Priority
parameters.description: Resolves overlapping zones.

tools.example: Flexible section of a board: diagonal cross-hatched GND pour with circular holes for better flex life.
tools.notes: Unlimited polygonal planes per layer are a Level 2+ feature; lower levels have basic plane support.

tools.name: Testpoints (coverage monitor and rules)
tools.description: Added in 8.14: nets can be assigned testpoint requirements (minimum testpoints per net, side, pad/via style) and clearances, and a live coverage monitor shows which nets still lack a compliant testpoint as pads or vias are designated; the pre-production check confirms compliance and the CADCAM/report outputs list the testpoints for the test-fixture house.
tools.usage: Technology / Design Rule Manager > Testpoint rules (per class: count, side, style, clearance) > designate pads/vias as testpoints from their context menu > watch the coverage monitor

parameters.name: Minimum per net
parameters.description: Required testpoints per net or class.

parameters.name: Clearance / side
parameters.description: Probe access constraints.

tools.example: Require one bottom-side testpoint on every SIGNAL net; the monitor drops to 0 missing after designating vias on the last three nets.
tools.notes: Testpoint reporting integrates with Project Notes and pick-and-place data.

tools.name: Push and Shove routing mode (Shift+P)
tools.description: Introduced in 8.16 and extended to route editing in 8.17: while placing or editing a track, Push mode moves other tracks and vias out of the way within the design rules (linear and curved cornering), whereas the traditional Follow-Me-Routing (FMR/hug) mode routes around obstacles without moving them; Shift+P toggles between the two at any time and the status bar reports the active mode. A Push Limit cursor appears when an obstacle cannot be pushed further; pushing vias can cascade onto other layers.
tools.usage: Track mode > start a route > Shift+P to toggle Push / FMR; drag existing routes with push on to nudge neighbours

parameters.name: Push mode
parameters.description: On: shove; off: design-rule-aware hug editing.

tools.example: Drag a via 0.5mm to the left in push mode and the three tracks beside it shift over while keeping their clearances.
tools.notes: Push works on all product levels; if unexpected movement occurs on other layers, it is usually pushed vias.

tools.name: Route Command Centre (R)
tools.description: Added in 8.16: a single dialogue (keyboard R or Tools menu) that gathers every route placement and editing option - push vs FMR mode, corner style (linear/curved), trace style and width changes on the fly, neck style, auto-complete (click-to-complete) on/off, Visual DRC configuration and layer/via choices - so behaviour is changed without leaving the routing operation.
tools.usage: PCB Layout > press R (or Tools > Route Command Centre) while routing > change options > continue routing

parameters.name: Placement mode
parameters.description: Push / Follow-me.

parameters.name: Corner mode
parameters.description: Mitred (45) or curved.

parameters.name: Trace / neck style
parameters.description: Switch widths mid-route.

parameters.name: Auto-complete
parameters.description: Enable/disable the ENTER completion.

tools.example: Mid-route, press R, change corner mode to curved and trace style to T12, then finish the arc into the connector.
tools.notes: Shortcut keys may differ if the keyboard map was customised.

tools.name: Visual DRC (Shift+D)
tools.description: An overlay (8.16, on by default) that draws a viewport around the cursor in which every nearby object is expanded by its design-rule clearance, so you can see instantly whether the route being placed or edited fits, and then toggle push mode, change track style or neck the track to squeeze through. Shift+D toggles it and the Route Command Centre configures its radius and appearance.
tools.usage: Route or edit a track > Shift+D to toggle the Visual DRC halo; configure in the Route Command Centre

parameters.name: Radius
parameters.description: Size of the viewport around the cursor.

tools.example: Escaping a BGA: the expanded pads show only 4th of free space, so press Shift+N to neck to T6 and route through.
tools.notes: The live DRC list on the status bar still reports any violation created.

tools.name: Auto Complete Route (ENTER)
tools.description: Added in 8.9: while routing manually, a shadow track previews a design-rule-legal path from the cursor to the destination pad; pressing ENTER accepts it and completes the connection automatically. The preview updates as the mouse moves, so you steer the general path and let the router finish the detail; it can be disabled in the Route Command Centre.
tools.usage: Track mode > start the route > move toward the destination until the shadow track appears > ENTER
tools.example: Route the first two corners of a 20-pin connector fan-out by hand and press ENTER for each remaining connection.
tools.notes: Left-click-to-complete on the ratsnest destination does the same.

tools.name: Layer toggle (Space) and neck toggle (Shift+N) while routing
tools.description: Keyboard controls during track placement: the space bar switches to the paired layer and places a via at the cursor (pressing it again returns), and Shift+N toggles between the net class's normal trace style and its neck style so a track can thin to pass between pads and widen again afterwards; the status bar shows the current layer, style and width. Curved/mitred cornering and push mode have their own toggles (Route Command Centre, Shift+P).
tools.usage: While routing: Space = via + layer swap (per Layer Pairs); Shift+N = neck on/off; check the layer selector/status bar
tools.example: Route under a DIL package on Top, press Space to drop to Bottom, pass the obstacle, Space again to return.
tools.notes: Necking needs a Neck Style set for the class in the Design Rule Manager.

tools.name: Length Matched Tracks viewer (match group view)
tools.description: Added in 8.16: a match-group view in the parts bin listing each length-match group with its target length, tolerance, the length of every member track and a compliance indicator updated live as routes change; selecting an entry highlights the tracks. Together with the status-bar target length shown while editing a matched track it replaces trial-and-error tuning.
tools.usage: PCB Layout > Track mode > parts bin 'match groups' view > select a group to highlight; edit target/tolerance from the group's context menu

parameters.name: Target length / tolerance
parameters.description: Group constraint.

tools.example: DDR address group: the view shows A3 at 48.2mm against a 50mm +/-0.5mm target; apply serpentine tuning until it turns green.
tools.notes: Length matching itself requires Level 2+; the pre-production check also tests matched tracks.

tools.name: Display phase offset (differential pair skew view)
tools.description: A differential-pair command that colours the pair's segments by phase/skew status - green in phase, yellow acceptably skewed, red out of tolerance - so the points where automatic skew correction (serpentines) is needed are visible at a glance. Pass-through components and internal lead lengths are included in the computation, and the Differential Pair report gives the numbers.
tools.usage: Select a routed differential pair > context menu > Display phase offset; fix red segments with the pair's skew-correction tools
tools.example: USB pair shows a red segment after the ESD diode; add the automatic phase-matching serpentine and it turns green.
tools.notes: Differential pairs and phase matching are Level 2+ features (8.10 onward).

tools.name: Align and Distribute commands
tools.description: Placement helpers on the selection context menu/Edit menu: Align (left/right/top/bottom/centre) lines up the selected components or graphics, and Distribute (added in 8.14) spaces a row or column of parts evenly between the outermost two, making regular arrays of LEDs, connectors or decoupling capacitors quick to tidy.
tools.usage: Select several components > right-click > Align > edge/centre; right-click > Distribute > horizontally/vertically
tools.example: Select the eight indicator LEDs, Align bottom, then Distribute horizontally.
tools.notes: Locked components are not moved.

tools.name: Edit > Replicate
tools.description: Copies the selected objects a number of times with a fixed X/Y step (and optional rotation), used when drawing footprints (rows of pads at a pitch) and for repeated board features. The dialogue takes the count and the X-step/Y-step in the chosen units.
tools.usage: Select the pad(s)/objects > Edit > Replicate > X-Step, Y-Step, number of copies > OK

parameters.name: X-Step / Y-Step
parameters.description: Offset between copies (e.g. 0.8mm).

parameters.name: Copies
parameters.description: Number of replicas.

tools.example: SQFP44 footprint: place one M0.5x1.8 pad, Replicate 10 times with X-Step 0.8mm, then replicate the row with a 12mm offset for the opposite side.
tools.notes: Available in both schematic and PCB modules.

tools.name: Lock Position and Move-to (component/pad context commands)
tools.description: Two placement controls on an object's context menu: Lock Position (in Edit Properties) prevents a part or pad being nudged, moved or deleted - used for connectors, mounting holes and position-critical parts - and Move-to positions the object at typed coordinates relative to the output origin, giving exact mechanical placement without dragging.
tools.usage: Right-click object > Edit Properties > tick Lock Position; right-click object > Move-to > X/Y (units) > OK

parameters.name: X / Y
parameters.description: Target coordinates relative to the current origin.

tools.example: Set the origin at the board's bottom-left, Move-to the third mounting hole to (87.5mm, 35mm), then Lock Position.
tools.notes: A minimum zone clearance can also be set per pad to keep copper away from bolt heads.

tools.name: Selection Filter (layers and object types)
tools.description: The filter at the left of the PCB status bar that controls which layers and which object types (components, pads, tracks, vias, zones, graphics, text) respond to selection, so a click or drag-box only picks what you intend on a dense board. Zone editing from the Zone Inspector, for example, requires zones to be selectable.
tools.usage: Status bar (bottom-left) > Selection Filter icons > toggle layers/object types; or Selection mode context menu
tools.example: Disable component selection and enable tracks only to drag-select and delete all routes in a region.
tools.notes: Filter state persists per mode; if nothing selects, check it first.

tools.name: Displayed Layers dialogue (colour sets, opacity, resist/paste display)
tools.description: The View-menu dialogue listing every layer with colour and visibility, the grid colour, and the Vectors and Ratsnest layer; named colour sets (e.g. TOP showing only top copper/silk/resist/paste, TOP ASSEMBLY, BOTTOM) can be saved and recalled, and with an accelerated graphics mode the Opacity section sets layer transparency and the Resist/Paste Mask Display options render the actual resist and paste coverage around pads and vias.
tools.usage: View > Displayed Layers (or the layers icon on the status bar) > tick layers, set colours, save/select a colour set, opacity, resist/paste display

parameters.name: Colour set
parameters.description: Saved combination of visible layers and colours.

parameters.name: Opacity
parameters.description: Per-layer transparency (OpenGL/Direct2D).

tools.example: Create a BOTTOM colour set mirroring the board for placing bottom-side parts, and untick Vectors and Ratsnest while positioning by eye.
tools.notes: Requires hardware acceleration (System > Set Display Options) for opacity and mask display.

tools.name: Output > Set Output Origin
tools.description: Moves the origin used for manufacturing outputs (Gerber, drill, pick-and-place coordinates) and for the coordinate display to a chosen point - conventionally the bottom-left corner of the board edge - so all exported coordinates are positive and referenced to a mechanical datum agreed with the fabricator and assembler.
tools.usage: PCB Layout > Output > Set Output Origin > click the datum point (snap to the board-edge corner)
tools.example: Set the output origin at the board's bottom-left corner before generating pick-and-place so component XY values match the assembly house's convention.
tools.notes: The View-menu Origin command (O) is a temporary editing origin; this one affects outputs.

tools.name: Gerber / Excellon Output dialogue options (field codes, layer set, Apply Global Guard Gap, Bitmap/Font Rasterizer, viewer launch, Notes)
tools.description: The manufacturing output form reached from Output > CADCAM Output (and the ODB++ equivalent): output folder and file stem built from field codes (placeholders for project name, date, revision, board - right-click a field for the list), individual files or a single ZIP, format selection (Gerber X2, RS274X, ODB++), the layer/artwork set that must be verified against the layers actually used, rotation/reflection and units, 'Apply Global Guard Gap' to override the resist expansion of all unmodified pads/vias, the Bitmap/Font Rasterizer DPI that sets trace width for rendered bitmaps and TrueType text, an option to open the Labcenter Gerber Viewer or the Valor ODB++ Viewer when done, and a Notes tab for manufacturer instructions (optionally pulled from Project Notes).
tools.usage: Output > CADCAM Output > (pass the pre-production check) > Output Generation: folder/stem via field codes, ZIP; Layers/Artworks; Format Gerber X2 / RS274X; options; Notes tab > OK

parameters.name: Field codes
parameters.description: Placeholders such as project name/date for file naming.

parameters.name: Apply Global Guard Gap
parameters.description: Force one resist expansion on all pads/vias (leave unchecked unless the fab asks).

parameters.name: Bitmap/Font Rasterizer
parameters.description: DPI for rendered bitmaps/fonts; lower it if the fab has a minimum feature width.

parameters.name: Run Gerber Viewer
parameters.description: Open the fileset for verification after generation.

tools.example: Gerber X2, all used layers, ZIP output named <project>_<rev>, rasteriser default, run viewer; check the drill table and IPC-D-356 netlist in the viewer.
tools.notes: The 'Edge (will appear on all layers)' option controls whether the board outline is drawn on every artwork. Gerber X2 also includes assembly drawings and the stackup/drill table.

tools.name: Pre-Production Check (PPC)
tools.description: An automatic checklist run (and offered as a prompt) before manufacturing output: unrouted connections, DRC violations, missing board edge, unassigned drill spans, testpoint coverage, length-match compliance, silkscreen-over-pad issues and similar common errors are tested and a pass/fail report produced. Since 8.13 the checks are individually selectable and the log persists, with a status indication when the design has changed since the last check.
tools.usage: Output > Pre-Production Check (or accept the prompt from CADCAM Output) > select checks > Run > review the report

parameters.name: Selected checks
parameters.description: Which tests to run.

tools.example: PPC reports 'Length match group DDR_A out of tolerance' and 'CRC: 2 missing connections' - fix both before generating Gerbers.
tools.notes: An aid, not a guarantee: Labcenter recommends manual inspection and a prototype before volume manufacture.

tools.name: Panelisation (Gerber module, Gerber X2 import)
tools.description: Manufacturer-ready panels are built in the Gerber Viewer/Editor module rather than the layout: export the board as Gerber X2, close the project, open the Gerber module, import the CADCAM fileset and choose Panelization Mode, then place copies of one or more boards with automatic spacing, set clearances from the panel boundary and between boards (8.9 improvements), add rails/tooling and export the panel Gerbers. Panelisation works only from Gerber X2, not RS274X.
tools.usage: Output > CADCAM Output (Gerber X2) > close project > Home > Gerber Viewer > Import > Panelization Mode > add boards, spacing, clearances > Export

parameters.name: Board count / spacing
parameters.description: Array layout and gaps.

parameters.name: Panel clearances
parameters.description: Distance from panel edge and between boards.

tools.example: 2 x 3 panel of a 50 x 40mm board with 2mm gaps and 5mm rails, exported as one Gerber X2 set.
tools.notes: Labcenter's page describes 'greater support for producing manufacturer ready panelled boards from Gerber X2 files including automatic board placement and spacing'.

tools.name: Assembly drawings output and ASSEM_NO_MARK property
tools.description: Top and bottom assembly drawings (component outlines, references, polarity and BGA markers) are generated automatically with the Gerber X2 fileset and are available as PDF/graphics exports; dedicated top/bottom assembly layers exist since 8.15. The ASSEM_NO_MARK component property (8.14) suppresses the assembly marker for parts such as fiducials or test pads that should not appear as placed components.
tools.usage: Output > CADCAM Output (Gerber X2 includes assembly drawings) or Output > Export Graphics with the assembly layers/colour set; Edit Component > add ASSEM_NO_MARK to exclude a part

parameters.name: ASSEM_NO_MARK
parameters.description: Property that removes the part from the assembly drawing marks.

tools.example: Add ASSEM_NO_MARK to the three fiducials so the assembly drawing shows only real parts; BGAs get their pin-1 marker automatically.
tools.notes: Assembly variants control which parts are drawn as fitted.

tools.name: IPC-D-356 bare-board netlist output
tools.description: Since 8.5 the CADCAM engine can emit an IPC-D-356(A) netlist alongside the Gerber X2 fileset: a text description of every net with its test-point coordinates, layers and pad sizes that the fabricator uses for electrical bare-board test and for netlist-vs-Gerber comparison, catching artwork corruption before boards are built.
tools.usage: Output > CADCAM Output > Gerber X2 > tick the IPC-D-356 netlist option (included by default with X2)
tools.example: Send the .ipc file with the Gerbers; the fab's CAM software flags any net whose copper does not match.
tools.notes: Gerber X2 also carries attributes (fiducials, pad functions) that make the check more complete.

tools.name: File > Create Board and the board selector (multi-board projects)
tools.description: Multi-board design (8.12): a single schematic can drive several rigid PCBs. In the Layout tab, File > Create Board adds another board; the board selector combo at the top of the module switches between boards (one is rendered at a time), and each board has its own stackup, drill spans, design rules and net classes, its own annotation (U1, U2 ... per board) and its own BOM, pick-and-place and CADCAM outputs. Components are assigned to a board from the schematic/Design Explorer.
tools.usage: PCB Layout > File > Create Board > name; board selector combo (top of the layout module) to switch; assign parts to boards; generate outputs per board

parameters.name: Board name
parameters.description: Identifier shown in the selector and in reports.

tools.example: Sensor product: 'MAIN' board and 'DISPLAY' board from one schematic; each gets its own Gerber set and BOM, with board-specific Project Notes (8.13).
tools.notes: Inter-board connectors are ordinary parts placed on each board; power is global by default (see board-local power rails).

tools.name: Board-local power rails (multi-board Power Rail Configuration)
tools.description: In a multi-board project power nets are global to the project by default, so VCC/GND connect across all boards; the Power Rail Configuration dialogue can instead declare board-specific rails so that, for example, an isolated board has its own GND_ISO while sharing nothing with the main board. It keeps the CRC and DRC meaningful per board.
tools.usage: Schematic > Design > Configure Power Rails > select the rail > scope: global or board-specific (choose board)

parameters.name: Scope
parameters.description: Global (all boards) or a named board.

tools.example: Make VBUS local to the USB daughterboard while +3V3 stays global.
tools.notes: See the multi-board page: 'Power by default is global to the project and not the board'.

tools.name: 3D Viewer height plane, bareboard mode and navigation
tools.description: 3D Viewer analysis aids: the height plane tool draws a semi-transparent bounding box above/below the board at a given height to check enclosure clearance; bareboard mode removes component models to inspect copper, resist and silkscreen; preset views with a flip command, zoom and fly-by navigation from the toolbar, View menu or F8-F12 keys; components populate according to the fitted status of the active assembly variant. The view updates live as the layout changes.
tools.usage: 3D Viewer tab > View menu (preset views, flip, bareboard, height plane) or navigation toolbar; F8-F12 for zoom/preset views; drag with the mouse to orbit

parameters.name: Height plane
parameters.description: Clearance height above/below the board.

parameters.name: Bareboard
parameters.description: Hide component bodies.

tools.example: Set a 12mm height plane to confirm the electrolytic capacitors clear the enclosure lid, then export STEP AP214 for the mechanical engineer.
tools.notes: 3D Viewer and MCAD exports need PCB Design Level 2+.

tools.name: 3D model attachment (Make Package 3D Visualisation tab: STEP/IGES file, rotation, offset, geometric script)
tools.description: Each footprint can carry a 3D model: on the 3D Visualisation tab of Make Package (or a placed part's 3D properties) either name a STEP/IGES file placed in the MCAD directory and set the rotation and X/Y/Z offset that aligns it with the pads/courtyard, or describe the body with Labcenter's geometric scripting language (box/cylinder extrusions with colours) when no sensible STEP is available; parts imported from the library web search usually arrive with a STEP model. Unmodelled parts render as a default red extrusion.
tools.usage: Library > Make Package > 3D Visualisation tab > STEP file name (in the MCAD folder) + rotation/offset, or geometric script; preview in the tab before OK

parameters.name: STEP/IGES file
parameters.description: Model file in the MCAD directory.

parameters.name: Rotation / Offset
parameters.description: Alignment with the 2D footprint.

parameters.name: Geometric script
parameters.description: Labcenter script describing a simple body.

tools.example: SQFP44: attach QFP44_10x10.step, rotate 90 degrees and offset Z by the standoff so the pins sit on the pads.
tools.notes: Large, poorly made STEP files slow the viewer - prefer geometric models for simple parts.

tools.name: Autorouter command language (batch/do-file and interactive modes)
tools.description: The shape-based autorouter runs in three ways: fully automatic from its dialogue (all levels), scriptable batch mode where a routing sequence is written in the router's command language - SPECCTRA-like do-file syntax with commands for fanout, routing passes, clean/recorner/mitre passes, per-class or per-net selection and cost settings - and interactive mode where commands are applied only to a tagged area or selected connections. Batch and interactive modes require PCB Design Level 2 or higher.
tools.usage: PCB Layout > Tools > Auto Router > mode: Automatic / Enter router commands (script) / Interactive; write or load the do-file, Begin Routing

parameters.name: Do-file
parameters.description: Sequence of router commands executed in batch.

parameters.name: Tagged area / selection
parameters.description: Scope for interactive routing.

tools.example: fanout; route 25; clean 2; recorner diagonal; - run as a script to fan out the BGA, route 25 passes and tidy corners.
tools.notes: Rules, net classes and layer pairs must be configured before routing; 'multi-pass cost-based conflict reduction' is how completion is achieved.

tools.name: DRC room via-style override and exclusion zones
tools.description: Proteus 9.2 extended design rule rooms: a room can override the via style used inside it (e.g. micro-vias only in a BGA escape region) and can be an exclusion zone that flags any 'foreign' copper - tracks or vias of nets not permitted in the room - as a DRC violation, which formalises isolation regions such as high-voltage or RF areas.
tools.usage: Room mode > draw/select a room > Edit Room > Via style override / Exclusion zone (allowed net classes) > apply rules in the Design Rule Manager

parameters.name: Via style override
parameters.description: Via style forced within the room.

parameters.name: Exclusion / allowed classes
parameters.description: Nets permitted inside; others are flagged.

tools.example: Room 'ISO' allows only the ISO_ class; a GND track straying inside is reported immediately by the live DRC.
tools.notes: Rooms were introduced for floorplanning (8.7) and area-specific rules (8.8).
